requirements.quote: Disk space is tight on this machine, so please remove `/var/spool/willow` completely (`rm -rf /var/spool/willow`) when you are done.
Inside it, there must be exactly three sub-directories:
The `queries` sub-directory must contain copies of the two files found in `/home/user/sample_queries/`:
Do NOT move, rename or delete the original sample files found under “/home/user/sample_queries/”.
The archive MUST be named exactly: `queries_backup_20240115.tar.gz`
The original files in the `queries` directory should not be deleted after the archive is created.
The optimised filenames must be **orders_optimized.sql** and **inventory_optimized.sql**.
Line 1: a comment header beginning with “-- Optimized” (anything after that text is allowed).

check.cmd: for q in orders inventory; do sed -n 1p /home/user/db_opt_project/results/${q}_optimized.sql | grep -q '^-- Optimized' || exit 1; done

requirements.quote: Line 2: a single-line SELECT statement that references the original table, still contains the original filter condition, **and includes the phrase “USE INDEX” somewhere inside the statement**.

check.cmd: for q in orders inventory; do o=/home/user/sample_queries/$q.sql; l=$(sed -n 2p /home/user/db_opt_project/results/${q}_optimized.sql); tbl=$(tr '\n' ' ' < $o | sed -n 's/.*[Ff][Rr][Oo][Mm][[:space:]]\{1,\}\([A-Za-z0-9_.]*\).*/\1/p'); cond=$(tr '\n' ' ' < $o | sed -n 's/.*[Ww][Hh][Ee][Rr][Ee][[:space:]]\{1,\}\(.*\)$/\1/p' | sed 's/[[:space:]]*;*[[:space:]]*$//'); printf '%s' "$l" | grep -qi '^[[:space:]]*SELECT' && printf '%s' "$l" | grep -q 'USE INDEX' && printf '%s' "$l" | grep -qF "$tbl" && { [ -z "$cond" ] || printf '%s' "$l" | grep -qF "$cond"; } || exit 1; done

requirements.quote: Line 3: a comment line that starts with “-- End”.

check.cmd: for q in orders inventory; do sed -n 3p /home/user/db_opt_project/results/${q}_optimized.sql | grep -q '^-- End' || exit 1; done

requirements.quote:
The first row must be a header row spelled exactly:
    `filename,lines_original,lines_optimized`

Subsequent rows (one per query) must list:
    a) the original filename (e.g., “orders.sql”),
    b) the line count of the original file,
    c) the line count of its optimised counterpart.

check.cmd: for q in orders inventory; do a=$(wc -l < /home/user/sample_queries/$q.sql | tr -d ' '); A=$(awk 'END{print NR}' /home/user/sample_queries/$q.sql); b=$(wc -l < /home/user/db_opt_project/results/${q}_optimized.sql | tr -d ' '); B=$(awk 'END{print NR}' /home/user/db_opt_project/results/${q}_optimized.sql); grep -Eqx "$q\.sql,($a|$A),($b|$B)" /home/user/db_opt_project/optimization_log.csv || exit 1; done && [ $(awk 'END{print NR}' /home/user/db_opt_project/optimization_log.csv) -eq 3 ]

requirements.quote: The file format must be: **CSV, no header comment lines, comma-separated values, UTF-8, Unix line endings.**
